{{Short description|Swedish chemist and professor (1936–2019)}}
'''Jan-Olov Liljenzin''' (1936-2019) was a [[Swedish language|Swedish]] [[chemist]] and [[professor]] in nuclear chemistry.

Liljenzin was professor at [[University of Oslo]], Nuclear Chemistry, [[Norway]] 1986-1989, and at [[Chalmers University of Technology]], Nuclear Chemistry, [[Gothenburg]], [[Sweden]], between 1989 and 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chalmers.se/chem/SV/amnesomraden/karnkemi/personal/jan-olov-liljenzin/downloadFile/attachedFile_f0/CVITASH.HTM?nocache=1187270554.03|title=Short Curriculum Vitae, Jan-Olov Liljenzin|publisher=Chalmers University of Technology|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323085154/http://jol.liljenzin.se/cvitash.htm|archive-date=2016-03-23|access-date=2017-11-07}}</ref>

Liljenzin made early contributions to the understanding of the influence of chemistry on core melt accidents<ref>{{Cite book |last=Liljenzin |first=Jan-Olov |url=https://www.nks.org/en/nks_reports/view_document.htm?id=111010111119435 |title=The Influence of Chemistry on Core Melt Accidents - Final Report of the NKA Project AKTI-150 |publisher=nka - Nordic liaison committee for atomic energy |year=1990 |isbn=87-7303-452-5 |location=Malmö, Sweden}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=RAMA Source Term Group - Final Report January 1985|url=http://www.iaea.org/inis/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/17/028/17028349.pdf?r=1|access-date=2017-11-07|volume=RAMA 85/3|year=1985|isbn=91-7010-063-2}}</ref> and participated in international research about iodine chemistry and how to mitigate radioactive releases from nuclear accidents.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://cordis.europa.eu/documents/documentlibrary/66627231EN6.pdf|title=Iodine Chemistry and Mitigation Mechanisms - ICHEMM Final Synthesis Report|last=Dickinson|first=S|last2=Funke|first2=F|last3=Cripps|first3=R.|last4=Bruchertseifer|first4=H.|last5=Jäckel|first5=B.|last6=Güntay|first6=S.|last7=Glänneskog|first7=H.|last8=Liljenzin|first8=J-O|last9=Cantrel|first9=L|publisher=European Commission|year=2003}}</ref> He also investigated various methods of treatment and separation of spent radioactive fuel as well as chemical aspects of final repository for radioactive waste.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.iaea.org/inis/collection/NCLCollectionStore/_Public/28/028/28028626.pdf|title=SKI Report 96:70, Risks from Nuclear Waste|last=Jan-Olov Liljenzin, Jan Rydberg|year=1996}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.skb.com/publication/22278/TR-04-15.pdf|title=Partitioning and transmutation - Current developments - 2004. A report from the Swedish reference group on P&T-research|last=Ahlström|first=Per-Eric|last2=Andersson|first2=Sofia|last3=Ekberg|first3=Christian|last4=Liljenzin|first4=Jan-Olov|date=May 2004|publisher=SKB - Svensk Kärnbränslehantering AB (Swedish Nuclear Fuel and Waste Management Co)|location=Stockholm, Sweden|id=Technical Report TR-04-15}}</ref>

Liljenzin was a co-author to ''Radiochemistry and nuclear chemistry<ref>{{Cite book|title=Radiochemistry and nuclear chemistry|last=Choppin|first=Gregory R.|others=Liljenzin, Jan-Olov, Rydberg, Jan, Ekberg, Christian|date = 8 October 2013|isbn=9780124058972|edition=Fourth|location=Oxford|oclc=859381735}}</ref>'' which 2013 was issued in its 4:th edition. He was a co-author to a number of scientific papers<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chalmers.se/chem/EN/divisions/nuclear-chemistry/staff/jan-olov-liljenzin|title=Publication list - Jan-Olov Liljenzin|publisher=Chalmers university of Technology, Gothenburg|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323085154/http://jol.liljenzin.se/cvitash.htm|archive-date=2016-03-23|access-date=2017-11-08}}</ref> about nuclear chemistry with applications to separation of nuclear waste and chemical processes during severe nuclear accidents. His publications has (2026) more than {{Nowrap|2 000}} citations and a [[h-index]] of 25.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-04 |title=Analyze Author Output - Jan-Olov Liljenzin |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7004589291 |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=Scopus}}</ref>
